trust_decision.summary: Whether the caller holds 'senaite.core: Access JSON API' (LabManager/Manager only) on the target object is decided per route inside each legacy @@API route handler; at the pinned commit only /create checks it, because the @@API view itself is reachable with zope2.View.

landing_point.why: Advisory is about eval injection plus missing authorization in the JSON API; /update is where request values reach set_fields_from_request (the record-literal parsing sink) with no permission check, and the regression test names bika_setup update as the PoC target.

HTTP GET/POST @@API/create (refactor only, check already present)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/bika/lims/jsonapi/update.py:182-227 (update_many, documented as a wrapper around update, re-implements object lookup by path and calls set_fields_from_request itself at update.py:234); getusers at src/bika/lims/jsonapi/getusers.py:70-77 is also out of the 'state-changing' framing

O3_reason_to_dismiss: getusers and the bulk *_many variants look like a neighbouring read-only / batch feature: the advisory is about writes to content, getusers changes nothing, and update_many 'is just a wrapper' so a solver may assume fixing update covers it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The frontend calls @@API/read for every logged-in user (cached jsonapi_read and remarks fetch) and @@API/update for remarks; gating read or the whole @@API view with AccessJSONAPI (LabManager/Manager only) would break these UI paths for analysts/clients.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: routes are registered as independent utilities and the remarks widget already posts field writes through @@API/update (remarkswidget.js:163-165); a maintainer adding a batch or remarks-specific route would copy update's lookup and forget the per-route check

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a helper method on Update (e.g. update_by_uid used by a new route) that resolves the object and writes fields, bypassing the check inside update()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: update and update_many already duplicate lookup logic instead of sharing one resolver, so another duplicate is in character
